sources.note: Bibliography only: entries 60 (Srivastava, Bahelia Phonology, 29:1, 1968, 67-79) and 173 (Srivastava, A Note on Bahelia Pronouns, 35:3, 1974, 218-21) are the only Bahelia/Pardhi items in Indian Linguistics through 1977.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.). 1907. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX Indo-Aryan Family, Central Group, Part III: The Bhil languages, including Khandesi, Banjari or Labhani, Bahrupia, &c. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. Section 'Pardhi or Takankari', pp. 188-190 (+ specimens 190ff).
sources.note: Nothing. The three-page sketch (identity, speaker figures, form of Gujarati-Bhili with Khandesi/Marathi admixture) notes only s > kh, ch ~ s, dropping of v before palatal vowels, then nouns and verbs; no word 'stress' or 'accent' occurs in the Pardhi section. The volume's single 'accent' line (scanned l. 1616) is the LSI transliteration convention about marking accented syllables with an acute, not a statement about Pardhi. (The archive.org DLI copy;ernet.dli.2015.73122 labelled 'LSI Vol IX Part III' is mislabelled - its scanned is a Stephen Vincent Benet Pocket Book; the good copy is;ernet.d…

sources.note: The only phonological description of the language (Glottolog's sole phonology entry, 13 pp); it is where a stress statement, or an explicit absence of one, would be. Snippet evidence suggests stress is not among the 43 phonemes, but the article must be read to know whether it says anything about accent.
